author: MabbuttR

title: "Better, Not Perfect"
body:
The focus on percentages to measure accomplishment in a day is THE crucial thing that makes this app great, because as someone who suffers from perfectionism and binary thinking it means that accomplishment becomes far more nuanced and relative - you're never thinking about the cliff edge of losing a streak or success/failure binary that then makes you feel like a failure,  discourages you from even trying and turns your behavior into fatalist protection from anxiety.

The flexibility of a percentage instead reinforces the idea of doing your best, it allows you to say, "hey I got 80% of the things i wanted to build habits for, that's pretty good for my circumstances today!", or "i have about 60% right now, is there something i could do to push that number a little higher?".  I get to treat my habit goals as a natural cluster of things to tend to beside my current life rather than a terrifyingly rigid law that slices through it, and i can still zoom in to still see the new habit ideas i'm not doing or having trouble with and figure out how to make that work.

There's other great features like the simple native UI, the full Apple Watch and Widgets integration and the option for a one time purchase, but the percentage focus and backseating of streaks made this a thing i actually use and bought over the hundreds of habit apps i browsed and dozen or so I attempted using.

My critiques are minor and mainly relate to laggy or non-existant background updates for complications on my Watch, the fact longer habit names get cut off in the UI, and the grouping system.  For groups id like to be able to see them more easily at a glance and define them in the Atomic Habits sense of "this is their purpose, this is what i'm trying to become through them", but the current filter system obscures and fences that sense of purpose off more than id like.

title: Not sure why there needs to be a subscription
body:
Don’t think this app offers anything over something like Streaks. 

Usually when apps charge a subscription they can often justify it by saying that your data is stored in your account for that service, which obviously takes up storage for the developer and server bandwidth and whatnot. However this app just uses iCloud to sync, which I already pay for. I don’t understand why I would also need to subscribe when all the operations of the app would be taking place on my device or through iCloud which I’m paying for, not the developer. 

The developer might say that they need to charge a subscription to fund development, but that only flys as a reason if the user expects frequent development and new features. Habit trackers don’t tend to need constant new features - there is a certain point at which an app becomes a good habit tracker. Development can be funded to this point through one time purchases. 

Hard to see the subscription model here as anything other than a cash grab.

However I started to get anxious by seeing my time lost in activities I didn’t care about, and got no motivation to achieve what I wanted during the day in the first place, as there is no real place to set goals… and that’s where Awesome Habits came in. 
Habits still allows me to time track an activity, but now not just any activity. It’s specific activities I care about and just those. 

The customer support is great too. I asked if it was possible to integrate Awesome Habits with other time tracking apps, via Zapier or IFTTT, or have access to to export/import functionality, and their was reply was really positive!

I’m looking forward to future developments. Thank you for making the app!

author: Richie00007

title: reliable, beautiful, well designed (a joy to use), affordable
body:
I have gone through a dozen habit tracking and time tracking apps, and purchased several also. 

This is the only app I've found which :

1.  treats time management at the same level as habits (eg ATracker buries goals in a separate page)

2. allows for timer & integer habits (incl 0 : yes some apps don't allow 0 as input lol, a necessity for tracking bad habit "unstreaks")

3. allows you to specify if a habit is good or bad (incl distinctly visualising that aspect)

4. doesn't limit the number of tracked habits (Streaks has a limit of 12 due to their design).

If you don't want to have to open multiple apps to track timer & goal based habits, then this is the best designed in that space. It is also more beautiful & fun to use than any other app I have come across in either field, which means it will get used daily :-).

App & touch performance is pro-level, and what users have come to expect, although some in this space don't tick either of those basics!

The non-subscription price of this app is in the middle of the range of prices for these apps. Which makes it affordable to all (thank you).

I give it a 5/5 score because it covers all my core requirements extremely well. As with all things, there can always be improvements, lol, so here is my wishlist for less important functionality (that could attract more users to it) :

1. tags to filter a long list of habits (the app does allow for distinctly coloured icons which almost achieves the same thing though)

2. tracking of start & end times, and allowing multiple segments in a timer-based habit (it could show the total, and then drill into the habit to show a list of segments : this would encroach on the time management apps' field!)

3. adding an overall note to a habit (it could simply be a single line of font size 8) to allow users to make a note of what they did wrong last time that broken their habit streak

4. there is some Apple HealthKit data which I don't use atm, but it could go even further (eg sleep hours, weight, etc)

5. there is one minor crash which can occur on editing the list for reordering habits (it rarely occurs, because I rarely need to reorder habits, and is therefore avoidable ... but the app instantly reloads with the same state anyway)

6. it's not mentioned in many comparative app review websites or youtube channels

Finally, my thanks go out to the clearly highly intelligent designer/developer for producing such a nice app, and giving us a non-subscription option.

title: Almost Perfect
body:
I like this app.

I like it a lot.

The interface is clean and very intuitive. The reporting is simple to read and it works across iPhone, iPad and Mac.

I have deleted many habit trackers and this one is staying and will be used.

It’s not there yet.

There are 3 things that I would like to see to make this app truly Awesome.

1. An Apple Watch version

2. Notes for each habit, though personally I see this as useful rather than essential.

3. Sort out the timer bug.

When using the timer, you have to leave the app open (in the background), with the habit open. If you don’t do this, the timer will pause.

As I say, the app is beautiful to use and very slick with some of the best widgets out there.

Consequently, it has become one of the most used apps on my phone.

If the developers produce a Watch version and sort out the timer then I’d give this app the full 5 stars.
